_comment: Tolerances for the equivalence run (tests/acceptance/run_recipe.py). There are no measured
numbers in this file on purpose: the thing this package is checked against is a the research code
run of the IDENTICAL configuration, and its values are written OUT to reference.json by the
harness rather than written down here.
WHY THE CRITERION IS THE DETERMINISTIC SERIES AND NOT THE PERPLEXITIES.
The anchor term is a Monte-Carlo estimate: n=16 hidden states are drawn from p(h) per site
per step. The two implementations draw them from INDEPENDENT RNG STREAMS -- the research code's
sampler passes no generator (src/lra_distribution.py:4272,4286,4305,4325) and so takes
torch's global default RNG, while lfa/sampler.py:55 owns a private torch.Generator seeded
from the config. Two full runs are therefore two draws of a stochastic objective, not two
evaluations of a deterministic one: bit-equivalence between full runs is impossible by
construction, and the difference between them is seed-scale, orders above bf16 kernel noise
(which is the smaller, secondary term). It is a wash rather than a bias -- same distribution,
same n, same lambda, same schedule -- so it points nowhere in particular.
WHAT THE CRITERION DOES AND DOES NOT PROVE. The step counts and the corpus counts are very
tight NECESSARY conditions, not proofs of identity: at batch_size=6, ga=1 a step count is
ceil(n_chunks/6), so a difference of up to five chunks in an epoch hides inside the ceiling,
and equal counts of chunks and tokens are arithmetically consistent with different text. What
rules that out is at the source level, and is recorded here because it is recorded nowhere
else: both loaders enumerate the corpus as a SORTED rglob over the same extensions with the
same skip-blank rule (lfa/corpus.py:233 vs the research code/src/data.py:390), both shuffle it with
the same Mersenne Twister under the same integer seed (lfa/corpus.py:269 vs
the research code/src/data.py:492), and both split at int(len(texts) * (1 - val_fraction))
(lfa/corpus.py:278 vs the research code/src/data.py:503). So the two runs see the same documents in
the same order, and the counts below are what would catch it if that ever stopped being true.
THE CRITERION (deterministic; these are what say the two implementations compute the same
thing, and none of them is resampled):
optimizer steps  = per-epoch global_step, EXACT integer equality on every epoch. One
comparison that covers the document set, the split, the chunker, every
epoch's chunk offset, the batch size and the accumulation window -- and,
since the schedule is a function of the step, the learning rate too.
corpus           = training chunks, held-out chunks and held-out tokens, EXACT. Where a
changed split, offset rule or sequence length would show -- a much
tighter condition than the same number of documents.
content_curve    = per-epoch training content loss, every epoch of the run, each within
tol_rel. Not the first few: the measured run agrees to 0.19 % at its
worst epoch and to 0.005 % at the last, so there is no window beyond
which the two 'drift chaotically'.
held_out_curve   = per-epoch held-out loss (the research code's eval.loss against the companion's
val_loss, the same token-weighted cross-entropy over the same text),
each within tol_abs_nats. Fifteen points on identical text.
THE INSTRUMENT ROWS ARE REPORTED, NOT ASSERTED (2026-09-07). domain_ppl and seed_drift are
the research instrument's two numbers -- direct_perplexity.overall.mean_perplexity over the
held-out chat-formatted Q&A set, and WikiText-2 drift over the full test split (window 2048,
stride 512) read against the base model measured in the same run. Each is ONE draw per side
of the sampled objective described above. They are printed with their deviations and carry
NO verdict: `kind` is "report" and `ok` is null, and they cannot fail the run.
Why they carry no band. They used to be asserted within 2 % (domain) and 1.0 pp (drift), and
the 2026-09-07 run consumed 1.95 % of that 2 %. But the spread of these quantities across
seeds has never been measured on either side, so a band on them was never calibrated -- it
was a number carried over from an earlier, paper-referenced design. Asserting an unmeasured
spread is the same defect as asserting a difference smaller than the noise of the thing being
measured, which is why the criterion moved to the deterministic series in the first place.
The remedy is not a wider band: it is a SECOND SEED on one side, which would measure the
spread. Until someone runs it, these rows are evidence a reader weighs, not a gate.
So: a large gap on an instrument row means INVESTIGATE (run that second seed). A miss on the
criterion rows above is the regression, and none of THOSE tolerances is to be widened to
accommodate a run: a number outside them is a finding.
